metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art doctor — the dispatcher case at art:117-121 that execs the ./setup script (a live-verification readiness checker), forwarding $@. setup is a bash 3.2-compatible script (macOS-safe) built around a check() helper that eval-writes dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars instead of declare -A. Two verbs on the command surface: bare './art doctor' (verify + print the FEATURE table + exit 0 iff all green) and './art doctor --install' (install Python deps + Remotion node deps + fonts + Kokoro model files first, then verify). Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification — importing every Python dep, actually running ffmpeg/ffprobe, and synthesizing + decoding a real Kokoro test phrase whose mean_volume must exceed -40 dB. A successful pip install by itself never turns a row green; kokoro_synth SPEAKS to earn it. Thirteen atomic checks aggregate into 7 FEATUREs; any missing atomic hint prints under the blocked feature. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workstation, section 3 captured with the Kokoro model file temporarily moved aside to force one red row. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 f659dd0dff9e9f3b05314570966e7535de3d4576a1af76487a9283d9553199f5.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case. Three lines, no aliases, execs ./setup with $@ forwarded.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file. Three lines: pattern doctor, exec the setup script if it's executable, forward every argument. There are no aliases. Every rule the command enforces lives in that one setup script.

show.event: code card fades in with 'art' in the title bar

props.title: art:117-121 — one branch, no aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # …
  doctor)
    if [ -x "$ART_HOME/setup" ]; then
      exec "$ART_HOME/setup" "$@"
    else
      echo "setup script missing"; exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  # …
esac

# The wrapper always: (1) resolves ART_HOME from art's own path,
# (2) execs the setup script if it's marked executable,
# (3) forwards "$@" untouched, so --install falls through.
props.sparkLine: One case. No aliases. One script.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK 2 — the two modes: bare verify vs --install-then-verify. The FEATURES table lives in setup.
beats.narration_text: Two modes. Bare art doctor: verify and print the readiness table. Add dash dash install, and it first installs the core Python dependencies, Remotion's node modules, the two bundled font families, and downloads the Kokoro voice model — then runs the same verification. Both modes end at the same seven-row FEATURE table. The install step's own exit code is reported, but never substitutes for a check.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the bash 3.2 compat trick. dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars via eval; the check() helper.
beats.narration_text: Under the hood, one small design choice makes this script portable. Macos ships bash three point two by default — no associative arrays. So instead of declaring an array, the check helper uses eval to write two dynamic variables per test: OK underscore ID and MISS underscore ID. That is why art doctor runs the same on a Mac and on Linux, without a bash five prerequisite.

show.event: card in; title reads 'setup:117-140 — check() and dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id>'
two example checks type below it

props.title: setup:117-140 — check() and dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id>
props.code:
# Dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars instead of associative arrays: macOS ships
# bash 3.2 by default (no `declare -A`), and this script must run there too.
check(){
  local id="$1"
  eval "OK_${id}=0"
  if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    eval "OK_${id}=1"
  else
    eval "MISS_${id}=\$3"
  fi
}

# Two examples — the first checks ffmpeg exists AND ffprobe exists;
# the second imports the Python module 'kokoro_onnx' from Python itself.
check ffmpeg    'ffmpeg -version >/dev/null 2>&1 && ffprobe -version >/dev/null 2>&1' \
                'install ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg / apt install ffmpeg)'
check py_kokoro 'pymod kokoro_onnx' 'pip install kokoro-onnx (the free voice engine)'
props.sparkLine: Bash 3.2 safe. OK_id / MISS_id via eval.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 2 — live verification, not receipts. Kokoro must actually SPEAK a phrase above -40 dB to earn green.
beats.narration_text: And here is the subtle part. Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification. A successful pip install is not enough. For the audio feature to turn green, setup runs setup underscore smoke underscore kokoro dot py, which synthesizes one real test phrase and checks that the decoded audio's mean volume exceeds negative forty decibels. A silent WAV is a failure. Kokoro has to actually speak to earn the green row.

show.event: card in; title reads 'live verification, not receipts'
the setup_smoke_kokoro.py summary types under it

props.title: live verification, not receipts
props.code:
# setup:137 — the kokoro_synth check row
check kokoro_synth \
  "python3 \"$HERE/runtime/scripts/setup_smoke_kokoro.py\"" \
  'Kokoro failed to synthesize + decode a test phrase above -40 dB —
   check model files, kokoro_onnx install, and ffmpeg
   (run runtime/scripts/setup_smoke_kokoro.py directly to see why)'

# What setup_smoke_kokoro.py actually does:
#   1. loads the onnx voice model from runtime/models/kokoro/
#   2. calls kokoro.create("brutalist smoke", voice="af_bella")
#   3. writes the wav, then ffmpeg -af volumedetect decodes it
#   4. parses mean_volume, asserts it is greater than -40 dB

# From the top of setup, in plain English:
#   Readiness is decided ONLY by live verification below — importing
#   every Python dep, actually running ffmpeg/ffprobe, and synthesizing
#   + decoding one real Kokoro phrase (mean_volume > -40 dB). An install
#   step's own exit code is reported (INSTALL_FAILED) but never substitutes
#   for a check: a green table means the checks passed, not that
#   `pip install` returned 0.
props.sparkLine: Kokoro must actually speak. Silence fails.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 3 — 12 atomic checks -> 7 FEATURES. Feature-level aggregation table; missing hint printed per blocked feature.
beats.narration_text: Thirteen atomic checks aggregate into seven features. Each feature is a pipe-separated line: the display name, then the atomic check IDs that must all pass. The main loop walks that list, and for each feature it collects the missing IDs. Zero missing prints ready. One or more missing prints blocked, then every fix hint indented below it. No red row goes to production without the fix line printing next to it.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the aggregation loop'
an example red row prints below it

props.title: the aggregation loop — setup:156-172
props.code:
fail=0
for row in "${FEATURES[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r name reqs <<<"$row"
  missing=""
  for id in $reqs; do
    eval "v=\$OK_${id}"
    [ "$v" = 1 ] || missing="$missing $id"
  done
  if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
    printf '  %-28s %b\n' "$name" "$(g '✅ ready')"
  else
    printf '  %-28s %b\n' "$name" "$(r '❌ blocked')"; fail=1
    for id in $missing; do
      eval "m=\$MISS_${id}"
      echo "        · $m"
    done
  fi
done
# …
[ "$fail" = 1 ] && { r "Something is blocked — see above."; echo; exit 1; }
props.sparkLine: 12 atomic checks → 7 features. One red → exit 1.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — hide the Kokoro model file; audio row goes red with two hint lines; exit 1. Recovery: --install re-fetches. Verbatim from demo/RUN-LOG.txt sections 3 and 4.
beats.narration_text: One failure worth showing. Move the Kokoro onnx file aside — the model is the one thing not in the git repo, because it's three hundred megabytes. Re-run art doctor. Audio row goes red. Two hint lines print underneath: the model files are missing, and the synth-and-decode phrase failed. Every other row stays green. Exit code: one. Recovery: put the file back, or on a fresh install, run art doctor with dash dash install. The exit code is the whole reason the command exists — a red row never ships a build.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art doctor. A live-verification readiness checker. One dispatcher case, one script, two modes. It imports every Python module, runs ffmpeg, makes Kokoro speak, checks the fonts, and prints the table. It exits zero when every one of the seven features is green, one the moment one is red — with the fix line printed underneath. Run this before you fill a beat sheet, and downstream failures with cryptic messages become failures with a checklist.

props.artifactHeading: art doctor — the whole surface, in the order you use it
artifactLines: bare invocation — ./art doctor [--install]; wraps the setup script with $@ forwarded.
two modes, one table — bare verifies; --install installs pip deps + Remotion npm + fonts + Kokoro model, THEN verifies.
live verification only — imports every Python dep, runs ffmpeg, makes Kokoro speak a test phrase above -40 dB. Receipts do not count.
13 atomic checks → 7 features — any missing atomic check blocks the whole feature and prints its fix line beneath.
bash 3.2-safe — dynamic OK_<id>/MISS_<id> vars via eval, so macOS's default shell runs the same script Linux does.
exit 0 all-green; exit 1 any-red — run this before a beat sheet, so downstream failures come with a checklist, not a mystery.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. props.segment: Read art doctor — diagnose without installing
props.command: From my brutalist.art toolkit root: (1) run ./art doctor and save the whole stdout+stderr to /tmp/doctor.txt. (2) Do NOT install anything. (3) For every row that says '❌ blocked', write one line naming the atomic check ID that failed (the id passed to check() in setup) and quoting the exact fix hint that printed beneath it. (4) If every row is '✅ ready', tell me the exit code and quote the one sentence the script prints under the table about what green does NOT prove. (5) Tell me whether you were tempted to run ./art doctor --install, and why you did not.
output: step 1 — stdout+stderr saved to /tmp/doctor.txt, nothing installed
step 2 — each red row mapped to its check ID + verbatim fix hint
step 3 — exit code reported and the not-a-render-proof line quoted
